payload.root_cause: Off-by-one in `Cart.subtotal()` at pyshop/cart.py:54: the loop `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)` iterates indices 0..len-2, so the LAST line item in the cart is never included in the sum. With 3 distinct products added in order (MUG-1 ×2 = $25.00, LAMP-1 ×1 = $39.99, PEN-1 ×3 = $3.00), only the first two lines are summed: 25.00 + 39.99 = $64.99, dropping the pens line and producing the reported $64.99 instead of $67.99. Any cart with ≥1 item under-reports its subtotal (the last line is silently omitted), which also corrupts `order_total`, which builds on `cart.subtotal()` (pyshop/cart.py:69). The correct implementation should iterate all items (e.g., `sum(item.total for item in self.items)`).
evidence: pyshop/cart.py:52-56 — `def subtotal(self)`: `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1): total += self.items[i].total` — the loop bound `len-1` excludes the final index, so the last LineItem is skipped.
pyshop/cart.py:37-43 — `Cart.add` appends new SKUs in insertion order, so the most recently added distinct product (PEN-1) is the dropped last element.
Arithmetic check: kept lines 2×12.50 + 1×39.99 = 64.99 (reported value); adding dropped last line 3×1.00 = 3.00 gives 67.99 (expected value) — exact match with the bug report.
tests/test_cart.py:21-25 — `test_subtotal_sums_all_lines` adds mug-1 ×2, lamp-1 ×1, pen-1 ×3 and asserts subtotal == Decimal('67.99'), encoding the required behavior.
pyshop/cart.py:69 — `order_total` uses `cart.subtotal()`, so the off-by-one propagates to discounted subtotal, shipping threshold, tax and total.
